name: Akebia Therapeutics, Inc.

profile.description: Akebia Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts nephrology company whose stated purpose is 'to better the lives of people impacted by kidney disease.' It markets Vafseo (vadadustat), an oral HIF-PH inhibitor for anemia due to chronic kidney disease in adult dialysis patients, and Auryxia (ferric citrate), which has faced generic competition from Teva since March 2026. Q2 2026 revenue was $49.1M (vs. $62.5M a year earlier) as Vafseo grew 60% YoY to $21.3M with more than 10,500 patients on therapy while Auryxia fell to $25.5M; the 2,116-patient VOICE trial stopped early in June 2026 after showing a statistically significant reduction in mortality and hospitalization versus ESAs. Vafseo's TDAPA add-on payment period ends December 31, 2026, after which Akebia plans to price it within the ESA range. The pipeline includes praliciguat (Phase 2, FSGS) and ebribafusp (Phase 2 basket in IgAN, lupus nephritis and C3G, data in 2027). Shares trade at about $0.71.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Akebia brought Vafseo from a 2022 complete response letter to U.S. approval and launch, building a new revenue stream that reached $21.3M in Q2 2026 (+60% YoY, +34% QoQ) with 10,500+ patients on therapy [1]; it is significant but not yet large enough to offset Auryxia's generic erosion. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found. Market Share (1/2): Vafseo is the oral alternative to injectable ESAs in U.S. dialysis and is now supported by VOICE outcomes data (win odds 1.16, p=0.0016 on mortality and hospitalization) [1], but ESAs still dominate the category. Pipeline (1/2): Named programs have dated milestones — praliciguat Phase 2 in FSGS (first patient January 2026, ~60 patients), ebribafusp Phase 2 basket with initial data in 2027, and VOCAL Phase 3b topline expected Q4 2026 [1][3] — but all are early-stage with no revenue visibility. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D of $62.4M was 26% of revenue [2], in line with commercial-stage specialty pharma.
innovation.label: DEVELOPING

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Akebia's purpose 'to better the lives of people impacted by kidney disease' clearly names who it serves [1], and the company has stayed in nephrology since 2007, but the wording is interchangeable with other renal-focused drug developers. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable foundation or quantified community program was found beyond the company's commercial products. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and Q2 2026 included a $1.9M restructuring charge to reorganize the commercial organization [1], following earlier downsizings. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP shows one open-market purchase against 15 open-market sales in Q1 2026 and one sale in Q2 2026 — net selling [5].
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (raw 0.57/10, rounds to 1). Debt-to-equity of 215.7% scores 0.37 [2]. ROE is deeply negative (about -119%, derived from FMP's TTM net income of -$0.110 per share and book value of $0.093 per share) and scores 0.0 at 2x weight [2]. Revenue fell 21.4% YoY in Q2 2026 (0.0) [1], and the FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR is -4.3% ($294.6M to $236.2M), scoring 0.05 at 2x weight [2]. The forward P/E is negative (about -5.0, derived from the $0.71 price over FY2026 consensus EPS of -$0.14) and scores 0.0, as does the -13.5% TTM net margin [2][4]. FMP's forward PEG of 0.0015 is an artifact of negative earnings and is excluded. Liquidity passes the floor at ~$5.5M of average daily turnover (7.75M shares x $0.71).
infrastructure.label: WEAK

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Akebia's revenue comes from FDA-approved physical drugs administered to dialysis patients; outcomes trials such as the 2,116-patient VOICE study and payer reimbursement rules (TDAPA, ESRD bundle) are regulatory and clinical barriers AI cannot bypass [1]. AI could speed rival drug discovery over time, which keeps this short of 9, but no analyst identifies AI as a threat to its earnings. AI Opportunity (0/1): Akebia reports no AI-related revenue.
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Akebia shows real persistence — nearly two decades in kidney disease and a willingness to fund a large outcomes trial for a drug the FDA once rejected — but it plays mostly a survival game. Repeated restructurings, insider selling, and a business shaped by reimbursement windows and generic cliffs leave little room for the trust and long-horizon courage that mark infinite players.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Better the lives of people impacted by kidney disease' is service-oriented, and the company has lived it by persisting with vadadustat through a 2022 complete response letter to approval and then running VOICE, which showed fewer hospitalizations and deaths versus ESAs [1]. The cause has not yet survived a leadership transition — CEO John Butler has led since 2013 [3] — so it stops short of 3.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Akebia has reorganized repeatedly, including a $1.9M commercial restructuring in Q2 2026 [1], and headcount stood at 194 at year-end 2025 [2]. Combined with persistent insider selling [5] and no retention data, the evidence points to an organization in cost-control mode rather than a strong Circle of Safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Akebia's messaging centers on defending Vafseo against ESAs and absorbing Teva's generic Auryxia [1]; no management commentary was found framing competitors as a source of learning.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The 2018 Keryx merger turned a single-asset developer into a commercial company with Auryxia, and Akebia has since added in-licensed assets such as praliciguat from Cyclerion and ebribafusp to diversify beyond anemia [3][6]. These are adjacent moves within nephrology rather than a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management kept funding the VOICE outcomes trial and pipeline studies through generic erosion and losses, a costly long-term bet that produced a statistically significant mortality and hospitalization benefit [1]. But the October 2025 decision not to run the VALOR non-dialysis trial was a retreat from a larger label, followed by a 32% one-day share drop [6].

investment_thesis: Vafseo is working: Q2 2026 net revenue of $21.3M was up 60% YoY and 34% QoQ with more than 10,500 patients on therapy, and the VOICE trial's early stop for a statistically significant benefit on mortality and hospitalization versus ESAs gives Akebia a differentiated outcomes claim to take to dialysis providers [1]. At ~$0.71 the company's market value is about $196M against $155.5M of cash at June 30, 2026, and management says cash, product revenue and a planned term-loan refinancing fund at least two years of operations [1][4]. Consensus models a return to profitability by 2030 (EPS ~$0.06 on ~$257M revenue) as Vafseo volume grows and pipeline programs in FSGS, IgAN, lupus nephritis and C3G read out from 2027 [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is a revenue cliff. Auryxia revenue nearly halved to $25.5M in Q2 2026 after Teva's generic launch, total revenue fell 21% YoY, and the net loss was $8.9M [1]. When TDAPA ends on December 31, 2026, Akebia plans to price Vafseo within the ESA range — far below today's price — so management expects Vafseo revenue to decline from 2026 levels even as units grow [3]. Consensus shows losses of about $36M in 2026 and continuing losses through 2029 [2]. Debt-to-equity is 216% with a term loan needing refinancing, book value is only $0.09 per share, and a sub-$1 share price exposes Akebia to Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance risk and dilutive financing (it sold $50M of stock at a 28% drawdown in March 2025) [2][4].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (early November 2026) showing whether Vafseo's sequential growth (+34% in Q2) continues fast enough to offset Auryxia's generic decline [1]

Presentation and publication of VOICE trial data (win odds 1.16, p=0.0016 on mortality and hospitalization), which could drive adoption by large dialysis organizations ahead of the post-TDAPA price reset [1]
VOCAL Phase 3b topline expected Q4 2026, and initial ebribafusp basket data in IgAN, lupus nephritis and C3G in 2027 [1][3]
key_risks: TDAPA expiry on December 31, 2026: Akebia plans to price Vafseo within the ESA range, which management expects to reduce Vafseo revenue from 2026 levels despite higher volume [3]
Auryxia generic erosion after Teva's March 2026 entry cut quarterly Auryxia revenue from $47.2M to $25.5M YoY, with further declines guided [1]

Balance-sheet and listing risk: 216% D/E, a term loan that must be refinanced, consensus losses through 2029, and a $0.71 share price below Nasdaq's $1 minimum bid that raises the odds of dilutive equity raises or a reverse split [2][4]
